as_told.title: Vallée's Passport to Magonia: the same phenomenon wearing cultural masks
as_told.place_text: Europe; Celtic lands; Ellsworth missile base, South Dakota

plain: The researcher Jacques Vallée argued in his book Passport to Magonia that today's alien encounters closely match the old folklore of fairies and elves. The writer Graham Hancock summarises the comparison for Michels without naming a source, though he credits Vallée and his own book Supernatural. In the old tales, he says, fairies and elves "would do surgery on people, they would abduct people, they would have sex with people, they would produce hybrid babies." That is the same set of things people now report from alien abductions. Michels returns to the book in a later episode and calls it "heretical to both believers and debunkers." He reads its argument as one phenomenon wearing different cultural masks over the centuries. He applies it to a 1977 case in which Air Force veterans at Ellsworth say they were taken by aliens. If Vallée is right, whatever people meet has been with us a long time and simply shows up in the costume each age expects.
